annotations.annotation_text: Universal archetype of the father and everyman protagonist Humphrey Chimpden Earwicker (HCE), manifested here as "hod". Represents the recumbent Dublin landscape with head at Howth and body stretching west to Phoenix Park.
sources: Glasheen, Adaline. Third Census of Finnegans Wake. https://archive.org/details/thirdcensusoffin0000glas

annotations.annotation_text: Satirical and biographical presence of Jonathan Swift (swift): Dean of St. Patrick's Cathedral, his dual lovers Stella and Vanessa (mirroring Issy), and his ferocious political satires.

annotations.annotation_text: The Book of Kells manuscript tradition (vellum): Joyce equates the text of Finnegans Wake and the Hen's letter to the labyrinthine Celtic interlacing and enigmatic Latin glosses of the 8th-century Gospel book.
sources: Trinity College Dublin: The Book of Kells Online. https://digitalcollections.tcd.ie/concern/works/hm50tr726

annotations.annotation_text: Ancient Egyptian eschatology (set): HCE as the dismembered and resurrected god Osiris, ALP as Isis gathering his scattered limbs, and the dream journey through the underworld (Tuat).
sources: Budge, E.A. Wallis. The Book of the Dead (The Papyrus of Ani). https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/1300
